messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: spatial models a la GeoBUGS?
parts:
Does anybody know anything about spatial models of the
variety implemented in GeoBUGS?

http://www.mrc-bsu.cam.ac.uk/bugs/winbugs/geobugs12manual.pdf

We had a request on the blog for implementing the
car.normal model.

This will be a nice background project for me, but if
someone else already knows these models and is interested
in coding them, I wouldn't say no to some help.

- Bob

messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] spatial models a la GeoBUGS?
parts:
I did not work on those models before, but learned a bit.  And I can help with it. 

What I am afraid is that some of those models are specified conditionally, remembering that once we have talked about directed graph and undirected graph.  So in Stan, if we can write down the analytical form of some distribution that is specified conditionally, it would be good to go.  Some simple model in Geo would be fine definitely, but not sure some complex one. 

--
Jiqiang

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] spatial models a la GeoBUGS?
parts:
On Thursday, February 7, 2013 11:55:57 AM UTC-5, Jiqiang Guo wrote:
I did not work on those models before, but learned a bit.  And I can help with it. 

What I am afraid is that some of those models are specified conditionally, remembering that once we have talked about directed graph and undirected graph.  So in Stan, if we can write down the analytical form of some distribution that is specified conditionally, it would be good to go.  Some simple model in Geo would be fine definitely, but not sure some complex one.

Now that we have the multivariate normal parameterized in terms of the precision, we are in a better position to replicate GeoBUGS models. The joint precision matrix often takes the form

A - rho * B

where A and B are constant matrices and the parameter rho is restricted to (0,1) or maybe (-1,1). There is often no alternative but to calculate the log determinant of that by brute force (QR decomposition or whatever) but the derivative of the log determinant with respect to rho can be worked out analytically, so we can do the calculations in doubles.

Users can do some of these models now in Stan code, but multiplying rho by B promotes to a parameterized matrix that is often large so the auto-diff will be a bottleneck.

Ben

messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] spatial models a la GeoBUGS?
parts:
I'd also like to point out the following:  if the model is specified conditionally so that the normalizing factor is hard to compute, this will be a challenge in Bugs well as Stan.  That is, even in Bugs, the normalizing factor needs to be computed (except in the special case that the model's hyperparameters are prespecified).  Neither Stan nor Bugs (to my knowledge) allows one to work with models with unspecified normalizing factors.
A

messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] spatial models a la GeoBUGS?
parts:
Consider two scenarios:
1.  Hyperparameters are known.  In that case, you don't need to specify the normalizing factor.  Either Bugs or Stan will work, you just specify the prior as an unnormalized density and all is fine.
2.  Hyperparameters are unknown.  In that case, Bugs and Stan both need the normalizing factor.
A
